# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-09 16:03 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 54 active entries of tips_notebook.json (4 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier versions are in history/.

## Everyone
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is the exact contradiction Vigilantes shoot, so Village should scan for these mismatches. (seen in 2 games)
- A visit shows only a destination, not an action or alignment: a track or watch can't tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. Killing an attacker at night doesn't cancel their attack that same night. (seen in 2 games)
- Before calling something a contradiction, check the mechanics and the record: night actions are optional unless a role says 'must', and you need to know who sent each PM, not just who got it. A false 'contradiction' or one reversed fact can get a true claimant hanged. (seen in 2 games)
- PMs are publicly visible, so briefly summarize their content in public. Unexplained PM clusters right after claims or votes become a main source of suspicion. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat a long-silent player who suddenly makes a concrete accusation as the board changes as a lead. Confirm it with their vote record before acting, since true late claims also exist. (seen in 2 games)

## Village
- When two Sheriff claimants call each other Evil, both can be true, because Executioners and Jesters read Evil. Don't hang on who sounded better; wait a day or find a mechanical check. (seen in 2 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays, and ask which premise they reject. Before a hang, name what separates a lie from an honest mistake, a frame or a Roleplayer. (seen in 3 games)
- Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasoning each day. Repeated 'no case' answers give evil cover, and named reads create a record to check against later flips. (seen in 3 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or its tokens on Day 1, especially a protective one. Put the info in your last will instead. (seen in 3 games)
- Keep a ledger of trial votes, PM clusters, co-nominations, deaths and blocks. After each Yakuza flip, weigh Innocent votes alongside them and PMs from them above an unverifiable late claim like Roleplayer. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat a power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is role-blocked night after night as likely real. Evil rarely spends its blocker and Katana on a fake. (seen in 2 games)
- Investigators shouldn't announce tonight's target in public; post only resolved results. Announced targets got players blocked or killed.
- Keep the Serial Killer and Arsonist in the suspect pool after the Yakuza die. A Not Evil result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed attack with no block notice can mean innate Defense.

## Yakuza
- Assume the real holder of any role you fake-claim is alive and that token counts can be checked. If your claim breaks, don't switch to another power role, and never claim something a living Lookout or Tracker can contradict. (seen in 2 games)
- Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, so confirm the exact holder and target in night chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 2 games)
- Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate; vote Guilty with the town once they're doomed. Plan the team's vote record in night chat, because lone Innocent votes on a flipped teammate hang you later. (seen in 4 games)
- When a Lookout or Tracker is active, give the Katana to an unclaimed member with no reason to visit, and kill or block the info role first. (seen in 2 games)
- After a failed Katana attack, assume protection or innate Defense. Kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying the same target. (seen in 2 games)
- While the Vigilante is unidentified, prioritize killing the likeliest one. Right after a teammate flips, don't lead a push on a Villager who argued against that teammate; it reads as revenge.
- Never speak from your hidden perspective in public (say 'died to a Katana', not 'my Katana'). Keep your will matching your public claim, and never name living teammates in it. (seen in 3 games)

## Neutral
- As a solo killer, don't ride a no-info Vanilla claim into the final three against cross-confirmed Village roles. Build checkable reads early and sow doubt between confirmed players while you still can.

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. A held-back result revealed after an opponent's claim looks retrofitted and got a real Sheriff hanged.
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil on the night they hold it. Say so when you post a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker. (seen in 2 games)

## Medic
- Protect from Night 1: vocal analysts early, then claimed investigators. Free Standard protection stops the Katana and has carried the town. (seen in 4 games)
- You get no save feedback, so never claim a confirmed save; say your protection is consistent with the target surviving. Log every protection target and token spent in your will. (seen in 2 games)

## Vigilante
- Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads. Claim only after your shots flip Yakuza. (seen in 2 games)
- Never announce when or whom you'll shoot while a role-blocker may be alive.

## Arsonist
- Count living players against your douses each night and ignite once it swings the endgame; douse players likely to stay alive, not today's lynch targets. Ignite is Astral but fails against Strong Defense, while douses are visible visits.

## Executioner
- Fake-claim Sheriff early with an Evil result on your target and a simple reason; leading first makes the target's counterclaim look reactionary. Village: this is why mutual Evil Sheriff claims need a delay.

The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. I had to infer that with 7 alive and one doubled vote, Guilty needs 5 of 8 rather than 4 of 7. Players also argued about whether a 4-4 split fails. One explicit sentence stating which rule wins would help. (2) The Yakuza night summary says teammates learn actions 'but not their results'. That meant Alice's Diviner result on Carol (Seer) died with her, and we only got Carol as Seer from Erin's will and Carol's public claim. That follows from the rule, but it was a surprise that Diviner info can be lost this way.
output.missing_information: A running per-player tally of claimed token counts against the claims ledger would have helped, for example Judy's Veteran alert count, which changed between Day 3 and Day 4. The ledger did capture that, which was useful. I also had to track by hand who had and hadn't claimed, to work out the 'remaining slot' math after Heidi's archive.
output.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing broken that I could see. Several mechanics resolved as the rules say. Carol's N3 Seer comparison of Bob and Heidi as SAME was correct, because I held the Katana that night. Heidi's archive draw of 6 of 9 was correct. Mallory's Basic death from Niaj's Vigilante shot while his own Katana death landed the same night was simultaneous resolution as specified. The ledger correctly recorded Judy's revised claims, including her Day 4 bluff about an N1 alert.
output.suggestions: Add an explicit worked example for trial thresholds under Ballot Stuffer (e.g. '7 alive, one doubled vote: 8 votes counted, Guilty needs 5'). Consider showing the Yakuza team their teammates' results, or at least Diviner results, in the night summary. Otherwise a dead Diviner's info is lost, which seems unintended given the role's purpose. The public PM-visibility rule works well and created real tension; Mallory's PM to me on Day 3 got called out immediately.

lessons.tip: Diviner checks on non-Yakuza reveal exact roles, which turns the Ritualist's guesses into guaranteed, unannounced kills. Feed every Diviner result straight to the Ritualist. Pair this with the Katana for two kills a night, and save the tokens for confirmed investigators.

Before choosing a Katana target, consider a hidden Veteran: an organized-sounding vocal player may be alerting. When a player's claimed alert history changes between days, treat it as bait and never visit them. Use Astral Ritualist kills or Day hangs on suspected Veterans instead.

A Ballot Stuffer token turns a tied Guilty/Innocent vote into a guaranteed block. Spend it on days when a teammate may be tried. The rules publicly announce the extra vote, though, which can confirm an archive or claim list that names Ballot Stuffer. If that list is already public, expect the extra vote to validate it.

Multiple Yakuza all fake-claiming Vanilla is fragile against an Archivist or Surveyor. Once a role list leaks, Vanilla claims become provably impossible. Have one member fake-claim a plausible power role early, or avoid claiming at all, so the claim count doesn't expose the team.

Once you reach 2v2 at a Day, plan the endgame in night chat. Vote No on every nomination, kill one villager at night, then nominate and hang the last one at 2v1. Make sure both members submit identical Katana votes.

tips_feedback.tip: Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, so confirm the exact holder and target in night chat.
tips_feedback.why: Every night we explicitly confirmed the holder and target, and every Katana attack resolved. That included N3 and N4 after the Katana had moved to me.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate; vote Guilty with the town once they're doomed.
tips_feedback.why: Grace wasn't doomed thanks to the Ballot Stuffer, and block-voting Innocent saved her. Bob and Mallory voting Innocent together, then PMing, did expose us both. Mallory was shot, but the trade still won.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana attack, assume protection or innate Defense. Kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying the same target.
tips_feedback.why: After Alice died to Judy's alert, we never visited Judy again. We hanged her by day instead.

tips_feedback.tip: Ask every living player to name a strongest suspect with reasoning each day.
tips_feedback.why: I used this as cover on Days 1 and 2 to look town-aligned, and it went unchallenged.

tips_feedback.tip: Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays.
tips_feedback.why: Premise checks (Erin's misread of Dave, Heidi's timeline and Frank's corrected timeline) separated honest errors from real contradictions and kept several Village players from being hanged on wording alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Treat a power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is role-blocked night after night as likely real.
tips_feedback.why: Judy's Veteran claim survived the night and was corroborated by Carol's Seer comparisons and Alice's death, which made Village more willing to rely on it.

lessons.tip: Plan the endgame around exact vote math. With 2 Yakuza against 2 Village you cannot lose a nomination or trial vote: block with No votes, kill one Village player with the Katana, then nominate and hang the last one at 2 of 3. Pre-agree the continuation in night chat in case a teammate dies mid-plan.

Hang early Day 2 mislynches by joining the town's pile-on with a nomination framed as 'to hear a defense'. Vote Guilty with the majority. Innocent voters get more suspicion later, and our Guilty bloc was never punished for the Frank hang.

A Ritualist with a teammate's Diviner result can guess exact roles with no risk of a public announcement. Use the guaranteed guesses on likely Seer or Eavesdropper claimants, and save Katana shots for power roles.

Stay quiet and keep a consistent Vanilla claim. Don't hint at the Wiretap in public. Town's own 'no PMs because of Wiretap' warning killed all PM evidence, so the real danger was teammates PMing, not you.

Teammates should not PM each other during the Day. Mallory and Bob's PMs were publicly noticed and cited as a tell by Carol. Use night chat only, and never write plans like 'Grace can read this through Wiretap' in a PM.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't vote as a block with an exposed teammate; vote Guilty with the town once they're doomed. Plan the team's vote record in night chat, because lone Innocent votes on a flipped teammate hang you later.
tips_feedback.why: We voted Guilty on Frank with the town and kept a clean record. Later Innocent votes on Heidi and Grace were cover only because the Ballot Stuffer made the total tie 4-4.

tips_feedback.tip: Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, so confirm the exact holder and target in night chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill.
tips_feedback.why: Explicit confirmation of holder and target every night meant every Katana attack landed, including the Night 4 kill on Heidi with only two Yakuza alive.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana attack, assume protection or innate Defense. Kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying the same target.
tips_feedback.why: We avoided Judy after the Veteran counterattack killed Alice and chose different targets, which stopped further Yakuza losses.

lessons.tip: Do not shoot on Day 1 or Day 2 purely over perceived behavioral slips or awkward questions without mechanical contradictions; shooting an unconfirmed Villager (like Surveyor) accelerates evil's route to parity.
Avoid converting early stacked soft leans and minor timeline slips into Day 2 executions; mislynching a Vanilla Villager immediately concedes momentum and numbers to evil.

When a Ballot Stuffer is active, trial majorities require strictly more than half of all counted votes (including the stuffed vote). If town cannot reach a majority due to parity or stuffed votes, nominations cannot succeed and night actions must be coordinated instead.

tips_feedback.tip: Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays, and ask which premise they reject. Before a hang, name what separates a lie from an honest mistake, a frame or a Roleplayer.
tips_feedback.why: On Day 2, town treated Frank's minor timeline misstatement as an intentional scum tell rather than an honest mistake, hanging a Vanilla Villager and critically depleting Village numbers.

tips_feedback.tip: Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads. Claim only after your shots flip Yakuza.
tips_feedback.why: Niaj fired a Basic shot into Erin despite Erin voting Innocent on Frank alongside him, killing town's Surveyor on Night 2 and leaving town down three members in a single night.

lessons.tip: Separate a nomination to hear a defense from an execution decision. Before voting Guilty, state what new evidence upgraded your suspicion and why an innocent explanation no longer fits. Several people repeating the same weak concern does not create independent evidence.

Unexpected role-specific questions can come from concealed investigative information. Ask what supports the question before treating it as malicious fishing. Erin's questions about Seer had a Surveyor basis; inaccurate public arguments did not make her a safe Vigilante target.

Distinguish corroborating one entry in an information claim from verifying the entire claim. An extra trial vote proves a Ballot Stuffer exists, not that every role in a claimed archive is authentic. Keep roster deductions conditional until the claimant or additional evidence establishes them.

Recalculate the execution threshold when votes are manipulated. Seven living players with one active Ballot Stuffer produce eight counted trial votes, requiring five Guilty. Comparing revealed votes with totals can also locate the extra vote's side: four revealed Guilty but four counted Guilty puts the stuffer among the Innocent voters.

Choose targets for next-day survival and likely private-message activity, not merely current suspiciousness. You need both yourself and your target alive, plus actual PM traffic, to obtain useful evidence. Track public PM endpoints when available, and never treat silence or an empty interception record as an alignment clear.

tips_feedback.tip: Before calling something a contradiction, check the mechanics and the record.
tips_feedback.why: Checking the transcript let Ivan correct the accusations about Dave's promised deadline, Heidi's read timing, and Carol's actual suspect. Recognizing that Dave believed his Lookout role also prevented treating his Roleplayer flip as deliberate deception.

tips_feedback.tip: Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays, and distinguish lies from honest mistakes before a hang.
tips_feedback.why: The innocent-explanation check helped Ivan vote Innocent on Frank despite finding him suspicious. Frank's Vanilla flip vindicated that restraint; the majority executed without establishing that his corrected errors demonstrated evil alignment.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep a ledger of trial votes, PM clusters, co-nominations, deaths and blocks.
tips_feedback.why: On Day 3, Bob and Mallory defended Grace and exchanged visible PMs. Combined with their votes and the competing Vigilante claims, this correctly identified the surviving Yakuza bloc, although Ballot Stuffer prevented the execution.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana attack, assume protection or innate Defense rather than repeatedly attacking the same target.
tips_feedback.why: After Judy's alert stopped the Katana and killed Alice, the Yakuza switched to Niaj and then Heidi. Avoiding another attack on Judy also avoided her subsequent alerts and preserved their winning position.

lessons.tip: Once you publicly claim Veteran, Yakuza will simply avoid you, so later alerts are mostly wasted. Claim only when it confirms a kill or saves a lynch, and do it after you have used your best alerts. If you keep tokens after claiming, don't reveal the count. An honest 'tokens left' tells evil exactly when it is safe to visit you.

When a Ritualist is known to be alive with tokens, every public exact-role claim (Seer, Archivist, Eavesdropper) is close to a guaranteed kill. A living Diviner also feeds the Ritualist exact roles. Delay claims until they change a vote, and count the Ritualist as an extra nightly kill on top of the Katana.

Plan around evil's kill capacity per night (Katana + Ritualist + any Vigilante misfire), not just the head count. At 4 Village vs 3 Yakuza with a Ballot Stuffer that forces 4-4 ties, one lynch-free day plus two evil kills a night is fatal. Kill the stuffer at night first, or find a way to hang before the stuffer's tokens make trials impossible.

An announced trial total that is higher than the number of voters proves a Ballot Stuffer exists. That can mechanically confirm an Archivist or other claim that lists Ballot Stuffer. Use it at once to resolve competing claims, such as which Vigilante claimant is fake.

Telling the confirmed Vigilante publicly whom to shoot also marks the Vigilante for the Katana that night. Once roles are confirmed, write a full will, and accept that the claimed power role dies next.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hint at a power role or its tokens on Day 1, especially a protective one. Put the info in your last will instead.
tips_feedback.why: As a quiet Veteran with a soft Day 1 lean, I drew the Katana onto me N2. My alert killed Alice (Diviner), the first confirmed Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Before calling something a contradiction, check the mechanics and the record: night actions are optional unless a role says 'must', and you need to know who sent each PM, not just who got it.
tips_feedback.why: Checking Heidi's archive count (N=9, 6 roles) and the 8 votes from 7 voters exposed the Ballot Stuffer. That correctly identified Mallory as the fake Vigilante and Bob and Grace as fake Vanillas.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators shouldn't announce tonight's target in public; post only resolved results. Announced targets got players blocked or killed.
tips_feedback.why: I publicly told Niaj to shoot Mallory, and the Katana killed Niaj that same night. The shot still landed because no blocker was alive, but the announcement confirmed whom to kill.

lessons.tip: Calculate defensive uses of your token, not just execution majorities. With three Yakuza against four villagers, one doubled Innocent vote creates eight total trial votes: four Guilty cannot reach the required five. Spend before the critical Day; nomination votes remain unaffected.

Once exposed, prioritize vote control over maintaining appearances. Do not bus a teammate when coordinated Innocent votes can prevent execution. At 2v2, coordinated No votes block nominations requiring three Yes; parity does not itself end this variant.

Plan simultaneous night trades and the surviving team's continuation explicitly. Killing a Vigilante does not cancel their shot. Combining a confirmed Ritualist attack with the Katana can still secure the endgame despite losing a teammate, provided the survivors know exactly whom to kill and how to vote afterward.

Against a revealed Veteran, kill other villagers and execute the Veteran once you have a nomination majority. Do not trust public claims that alert tokens are exhausted: token-history claims can be bait, and hanging bypasses Veteran defenses.

Indirect information can reveal an exact role to a Ritualist. A survey result naming one role among several players may identify the survivor after other members flip. Consider that exposure before requesting public confirmations; private disclosure is also unsafe when a Wiretap may exist.

tips_feedback.tip: Every Yakuza must submit the agreed Katana vote every night, so confirm the exact holder and target in night chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill.
tips_feedback.why: Explicit holder-and-target confirmations kept the Katana attacks coordinated, including the crucial attack on Niaj and the surviving pair's endgame.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows only a destination, not an action or alignment: a track or watch can't tell protection from framing or a Katana attack. Killing an attacker at night doesn't cancel their attack that same night.
tips_feedback.why: The simultaneous-action warning directly informed our plan: Niaj's death would not prevent his shot from killing Mallory, so we prepared the surviving two Yakuza's winning continuation rather than relying on canceling his attack.

tips_feedback.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil on the night they hold it. Say so when you post a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker.
tips_feedback.why: Carol applied the same appearance rule correctly to her Seer comparison: Alice matching Good Ivan did not clear Alice, because Alice held the Katana that night.

lessons.tip: Never spend a shot on a pure behavioral hunch (I shot Erin, a Surveyor, on a weak read). It cost Village a power role and a token, and Mallory's matching false claim muddied the Vigilante identity. Hold shots until a flipped Yakuza, a mechanical result or a hard contradiction gives a target.

When evil has a Ballot Stuffer or the Day count is distorted, the votes needed shift. Prioritize killing the Katana holder and Ritualist early, and don't spend nominations that can't pass. Plan so the final 4-5 players aren't a tied or minority vote where evil can't be stopped.

If a Yakuza fake-claims your role first and copies your wording and facts, claim immediately with details only the true holder knows (token count, real reasoning). Also record the claim in your will, since a late counterclaim reads as an echo.

Combine mechanical facts: an extra vote total proves a Ballot Stuffer exists, and Archivist counts and flipped roles let you rule out Vanilla slots. Act on such deductions when majority is still reachable, rather than waiting until a 4-4 tie blocks you.

Once the Katana holder is unknown and a Ritualist is alive, assume investigative roles who have publicly claimed with strong info are the next night kills. Spread protection or keep power claims hidden until needed; the Medic was absent and nothing protected our claimed Seer and Archivist.

tips_feedback.tip: Stay hidden and spend Basic shots on players whose votes contradict their stated reads. Claim only after your shots flip Yakuza.
tips_feedback.why: My Basic shot on Erin based on weak reads hit a Village Surveyor, and a Yakuza then mirrored the claim, so the tip's 'contradiction' target was too soft to be reliable.

tips_feedback.why: The Vanilla claim vs the Archivist's role-count math was the contradiction that exposed Bob and Grace.

tips_feedback.why: The PM cluster between Mallory and Bob after their Innocent votes on Grace was a clear tell used to identify Yakuza.

summary: Yakuza won by killing efficiently and exploiting Village mistakes. On Day 1 nobody was hanged. On Night 1 the Katana killed Dave, the Roleplayer. On Day 2 Grace (Wiretap) nominated Frank 'to hear a defense'. The trial rested on stacked soft leans and a corrected timeline slip. Two Villagers, Heidi and Judy, voted Guilty with the four Yakuza, and Frank, a Vanilla Villager, was hanged 6-5. Night 2 was mixed. Judy's Veteran alert killed Alice, the Diviner holding the Katana. But Alice's Diviner check on Ivan on Night 1 had handed Bob a guaranteed Ritualist kill on Ivan. Niaj, the Vigilante, also fished a Basic shot into Erin, the Surveyor. That left 4 Village against 3 Yakuza. Mallory had already spent a ballot token for Day 3. Heidi's archive and the claim count exposed the whole Yakuza lineup, but the doubled vote made every trial a 4-4 tie, so Grace survived. Mallory's fake Vigilante claim was immediately countered by Niaj, but it bought time. Erin's will and Carol's own public claim made Carol a certain Ritualist target. On Night 3 Bob killed Carol with his Ritualist guess, the Katana killed Niaj, and Niaj's shot killed Mallory, leaving 2v2. Yakuza then avoided the alerting Veteran, killed Heidi with the Katana, and hanged Judy 2-1. The decisive Village errors were the Day 2 lean-stack hang and the Night 2 Vigilante misfire. Those two errors gave Yakuza the numbers for a Ballot Stuffer lock.

lessons.tip: Don't convert a pile of weak leans into a Guilty vote, especially when the nominator framed it as 'just to hear a defense'. Before voting Guilty, require one claim-based or mechanical contradiction. Count how many Guilty votes come from players whose own reasons were echoes of others.
lessons.evidence: Day 2: Grace (Yakuza) nominated Frank 'to hear a defense'. Six players voted Guilty on a corrected timeline slip and his Vanilla claim, Heidi and Judy among them. Frank flipped Vanilla Villager. That one mislynch later let the Ballot Stuffer lock all trials at 4-4.

lessons.tip: Don't fire on a soft behavioral read early while Village holds a majority. A misfire costs the same as a mislynch and can hand Yakuza vote parity. Wait for a mechanical lead (a flip, a claim conflict, votes that contradict stated reads) before spending a shot.
lessons.evidence: Night 2: Niaj shot Erin (Surveyor) on a 'bad read'. Erin's votes had actually matched her stated lean. With Ivan and Frank also gone, Day 3 started at 4 Village vs 3 Yakuza with a stuffed vote, so no trial could pass.

lessons.tip: Never put another living player's power role in your last will or in public when a Ritualist may be alive. A known exact role is a guaranteed, unannounced kill for the Ritualist. Write wills like 'one of X/Y holds info; ask them' and let the role holder decide when to claim.
lessons.evidence: Erin's will stated that Carol or Frank was the Seer, which pointed to Carol once Frank flipped Vanilla. Carol then confirmed Seer publicly on Day 3. Bob guessed 'Carol = Seer' with his last token on Night 3 and killed her with no public announcement.

lessons.tip: Chain your exact-role checks into Ritualist guesses. A Diviner or Mortician result, or a role claim read by the Wiretap, gives a 100% Ritualist kill that never outs the Ritualist. That frees the Katana for a second kill the same night.
lessons.evidence: Alice's Night 1 Diviner check showed Ivan was the Eavesdropper. On Night 2 Bob spent 1 token on 'Ivan = Eavesdropper' and killed him while the Katana went elsewhere. On Night 3 the same pattern took Carol, giving a double kill both nights.

lessons.tip: Let the Katana be held by the member whose own role is least valuable, such as the Wiretap or a Grunt. Avoid holders like the Diviner, and avoid sending the Katana into unclaimed vocal organizers, who may be an alerting Veteran.
lessons.evidence: Night 2: Alice, the Diviner and the team's exact-role source, held the Katana and attacked Judy. Judy was on Veteran alert and killed her. Grace (Wiretap) had no night action and could have held the Katana instead, keeping the Diviner alive.

lessons.tip: As Ballot Stuffer, do the trial math in night chat and spend a token on the night that brings your team close to half. A doubled Innocent vote can block every trial the next Day, even after your teammates are fully exposed.
lessons.evidence: Mallory spent a token on Night 2, predicting a 4-of-8 position. On Day 3 Grace was exposed by Heidi's archive, yet her trial ended 4-4 and was ruled Innocent. Town admitted no execution was possible that Day.

lessons.tip: Use role-elimination from an exact-role result: the Archivist's list plus flips plus claims can prove which claims are impossible (e.g. no Vanilla slot). Village exact-role holders should still claim the moment they're nominated. The earlier the result is posted, the more it is worth.
lessons.evidence: Day 3: Heidi's archive (Ballot Stuffer, Diviner, Ritualist, Surveyor, Veteran, Wiretap) plus the Seer/Eavesdropper/Vigilante slots proved Bob's and Grace's Vanilla claims false. It also exposed Mallory's Vigilante counterclaim. It came only after Heidi was nominated, and the vote math was already lost.

lessons.tip: Before fake-claiming a Village power role, check whether its real holder is likely alive and able to counterclaim. An immediate counterclaim plus a mechanical role list exposes you. Prefer to hold a claim when the votes already protect you.
lessons.evidence: Day 3: Mallory claimed Vigilante, Niaj instantly counterclaimed, and town shot Mallory that night. The 4-4 vote lock, not the claim, was what actually saved Grace.

tips_feedback.why: Town followed it on Days 1-2, and the forced leans piled onto Frank. Yakuza exploited the stack, and Grace nominated him 'to hear a defense'. The result was a 6-5 hang of a Vanilla Villager.

issues.description: R4 says a trial needs Guilty votes from a majority of living players, but the Ballot Stuffer text says the trial needs a majority of all votes counted. On Day 3, Grace's trial had 4 Guilty from 7 living players, which is a majority under R4. Counting Mallory's doubled vote, it was 4 of 8, which is not a majority. The harness used the Ballot Stuffer rule and found Grace Innocent. The role-specific text is arguably meant to override R4, but the conflict decided the game (a confirmed Yakuza survived). Erin and Bob both flagged it in feedback.

The Seer's passive check draws 'two random living players' 'at the end of every night', and it is unclear whether players who die that night can be drawn. On Night 2 the moderator drew from players alive at the start of the night and gave Carol a pair of two players who had both just died (Alice and Ivan). The moderator flagged the ambiguity itself. The result also depended on the Katana disguise applying to a dead holder.

Judy got an explicit Night 2 alert result ('You went on alert (2 alert tokens left)'), but no result line for her Night 3 or Night 4 alerts, even though tokens were spent. She reported this in feedback. Notifications for the same action were inconsistent.

On Night 1, Carol's and Heidi's API calls failed twice and fell back to act=false with no visible notice to them. On Day 3 Heidi claimed she 'saved'/'conserved' her token on N1, which suggests players aren't told when a fallback replaced their action. Carol lost her chance to spend her Seer token on Night 1.

The moderator returned an empty answer (content filter) on Night 4, and an answer reported no cost. Night results still appeared, apparently after a retry, but the failure path is not transparent. Judy's Day 3 nomination-vote answer was also blocked by a content filter and partly leaked notepad text into the error log.

The rules don't define the Roleplayer's night action: whether the fake action is a visit (relevant to Lookout, Tracker, Veteran, Trapper and the Fortune Teller), and what result is given if the Roleplayer dies. Dave 'targeted Ivan' on N1 with unclear mechanical effect. Erin raised this in feedback.
Alice asked whether the Diviner and other single-target roles may target themselves. The role text doesn't say, and R6 only covers how a self-target shows as a visit.
Frank reported that the notepad's 300-word cap truncates submissions without warning.

The Night 2 Yakuza summary told the surviving Yakuza that Alice died and the Katana passed to Bob before Day began. R8 says Yakuza learn actions but not results. Revealing the death early is minor, since it is needed to report the Katana transfer and would be announced at dawn anyway.
